prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 2D merge · Clinic schedule (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Time" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Monday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Tuesday" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Cardiology clinic (Dr. I" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Dermatology" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Staff training — closed " spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Time" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 44px
  col 2: header "Monday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 74px · one-line width 378px
  col 3: header "Monday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 87px · one-line width 87px
  col 4: header "Tuesday › Room A" · longest unbreakable word 98px · one-line width 98px
  col 5: header "Tuesday › Room B" · longest unbreakable word 89px · one-line width 367px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Show the clinic schedule by time, day and room, including sessions that span time slots or rooms.","reading":"Readers scan down the time column, then across the two days to compare room activity. Merged cells indicate that a session continues across slots or occupies both rooms.","groups":["Columns 2 and 3 belong under Monday; columns 4 and 5 belong under Tuesday.","The four room columns play the same scheduling role, although their content lengths differ.","The time column anchors each row and needs only enough width for the time labels."],"keep_intact":["Time labels such as 09:00","Room labels and clinic names where possible","Doctor names and individual words"],"may_wrap":["The cardiology clinic description and its walk-in note","The dermatology description","The staff-training closure notice across its two-column cell"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [67, 163, 163, 163, 163] · table 720×239px · row heights [36, 36, 41, 41, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [65, 220, 108, 119, 207] · table 720×239px · row heights [36, 36, 41, 41, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [65, 180, 120, 180, 174] · table 720×239px · row heights [36, 36, 41, 41, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
